title: Sweet Wines of the World
description: The great sweet wines, how each is made and why they last for decades.
L: Explain how botrytis changes the grape
Explain why botrytis wines are hard to make

Botrytis cinerea pierces the grape skin with fine filaments. Water evaporates, concentrating sugar and acid. The fungus also consumes some acid and sugar, and produces glycerol, which adds viscosity, and gluconic acid. It creates new aromas: honey, apricot, marmalade, saffron and ginger. Laccase, an enzyme it produces, makes the juice prone to oxidation.

Infection is uneven and weather-dependent. In bad years, botrytis doesn't come, or grey rot does. Pickers make several passes, called tries, taking only affected berries. Yields can fall to 10 hl/ha or less. Fermentation of such sweet juice is slow, sometimes months, and stops naturally around 13 to 14% alcohol, leaving 100 g/l or more of sugar.
Several passes, tiny yields, slow fermentation
Why do pickers pass through botrytis vineyards several times?
Infection is uneven, so only affected berries are picked each time
Botrytis spreads unevenly. Each pass, or trie, takes only the berries that are ready.

Botrytised juice is low in yeast nutrients and high in sugar, stressing the yeast. It produces more volatile acidity than normal, so legal limits are higher for these wines. SO2 is needed to protect against laccase and to stop fermentation at the right moment. Many wines then age in oak for 18 to 36 months.
Which are effects of noble rot on grapes?
Botrytis weakens and pierces skins rather than thickening them.
Botrytis concentrates the grape and adds new aromas
Uneven infection means several passes and tiny yields
Fermentation is slow, stressed and needs SO2 to stop it

Sauternes and Barsac lie in southern Graves, where the cool Ciron river meets the warmer Garonne. In autumn, this temperature difference creates morning mist, then sunny afternoons, ideal for noble rot. Barsac, on flatter limestone, can label its wines as Barsac or Sauternes.

Sémillon is about 80% of plantings: thin skins welcome botrytis and give body and honey. Sauvignon Blanc adds acidity and freshness; Muscadelle adds perfume. Wines ferment and age in barrels, often new, for 18 to 36 months. Alcohol is around 13 to 14%, sugar 100 to 150 g/l. Good Sauternes ages for decades.
Sémillon's thin skins make it the ideal host for noble rot.

In 1855, Sauternes and Barsac were classified alongside the Médoc. Château d'Yquem was given the unique rank of Premier Cru Supérieur. Below it are 11 Premiers Crus, like Climens and Suduiraut, and 15 Deuxièmes Crus. Yquem may not make Sauternes in poor years; it skipped 1992, for example.
Château d'Yquem holds a unique rank in the 1855 classification.
Yes. It is the only Premier Cru Supérieur.
The Ciron's mists bring noble rot to Sauternes and Barsac
Sémillon leads, with Sauvignon and Muscadelle, aged in oak
Yquem is the only Premier Cru Supérieur of 1855
Explain how Aszú is made in detail

Aszú berries, shrivelled by botrytis, are picked one by one and stored as a paste. They're added to a base wine or fermenting must, soaked for 12 to 60 hours, then pressed. Traditionally, sweetness was measured in puttonyos, the number of 25 kg baskets of aszú per 136-litre barrel. Since 2013, Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar.

Szamorodni, meaning as it comes, is made from whole bunches with some aszú berries, not separated. It can be dry, aged under a flor-like yeast, or sweet. Eszencia is the free-run juice that drips from aszú berries under their own weight. It can have over 450 g/l of sugar, ferments for years, and rarely reaches 5% alcohol.
Match each Tokaji to its making.
Tokaj makes several wines from the same harvest.

Tokaji Aszú ages at least 18 months in oak, traditionally small Gönci barrels of 136 litres, in cellars cut into volcanic rock, lined with a black mould, Zasmidium cellare, that regulates humidity. High acidity from Furmint lets these wines age for a century or more.
Tokaji ____ is the free-run juice from aszú berries.
Eszencia is so sweet it ferments very slowly and stays very low in alcohol.
Aszú berries are soaked in base wine, giving at least 120 g/l of sugar
Szamorodni uses whole bunches; Eszencia is pure free-run juice
Furmint's acidity lets Tokaji age for a century

Germany's Prädikat levels start with Kabinett and Spätlese, which can be dry or sweet. The sweet wines rise from there. Auslese comes from selected very ripe bunches, sometimes with botrytis. Beerenauslese, BA, uses individually selected overripe berries, usually botrytised. Trockenbeerenauslese, TBA, uses dried, shrivelled botrytis berries, with a minimum of 150 to 154 degrees Oechsle. Eiswein uses frozen grapes.

Riesling's acidity, often 8 to 12 g/l in TBA, balances sugar that can exceed 300 g/l. Alcohol can be as low as 5.5 to 8%. This tension between sugar and acid is what lets German sweet wines feel lively, and lets them age for decades. Without acidity, they'd be syrupy.
Order these Prädikat levels from least to most concentrated.
Each level requires riper, more concentrated grapes. Only the top two rely on individually picked, usually botrytised berries.

Austria's sweet wines centre on Burgenland's Neusiedlersee, a large, shallow lake whose humidity favours noble rot almost every year. Rust's Ausbruch, a historic style between BA and TBA, is revived as Ruster Ausbruch. Welschriesling, Chardonnay and Scheurebe are common grapes for TBA there.
Not true. Trocken here refers to dried berries, not dryness. TBA is among the sweetest wines in the world.
Germany's sweet Prädikats rise from Auslese to TBA
Riesling's acidity balances sugar over 300 g/l
Austria's Neusiedlersee makes TBA and Ruster Ausbruch

Ice wine grapes must freeze naturally on the vine, usually at minus 7 to minus 13 degrees, often in December or January. Picking happens at night while frozen. The press releases only small amounts of concentrated juice, sometimes 15% of normal. Canada uses Vidal and Riesling; Germany and Austria use mainly Riesling.

Passito wines are made from grapes dried after harvest. Methods vary: on straw mats, in ventilated lofts, or hanging. Vin Santo is dried for months, then aged for years in small, sealed barrels called caratelli, with some oxidation. Passito di Pantelleria uses Zibibbo, a Muscat, dried in the sun.
Dried on mats, lofts or racks
Match each wine to its method.
Different traditions concentrate sugar in different ways.
Vin Santo with cantucci biscuits is a Tuscan ritual: dip the biscuit in the wine. The wine's nutty, dried fruit notes match the almonds.
Why is ice wine picked at night?
Grapes must stay frozen until pressed so the water remains as ice.
Ice wine grapes freeze naturally and are pressed while frozen
Passito grapes are dried after picking
Vin Santo, Recioto and Pantelleria are classic passito wines

Compare the great sweet wine traditions
Match each wine to its country.
Each country has its own great sweet wine.
What is a trie in Sauternes?
A pass through the vineyard to pick botrytised grapes
Pickers make several tries, taking only the berries that are ready.
Which wines rely mainly on noble rot?
Icewine relies on freezing, not botrytis.
Eszencia often reaches only around 5% alcohol or less.
Yes. With over 450 g/l of sugar, it ferments very slowly and stays very low in alcohol.
Château d'Yquem is the only ____ Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification.
Yquem holds the unique rank of Premier Cru Supérieur.
Botrytis concentrates sugar and adds honeyed aromas
Sauternes, Tokaji and German TBA are botrytis wines
Ice wine and passito use frost and drying
High acidity keeps all great sweet wines fresh
